# Enemy design UI covers Gym scene buttons (AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF)

## Headline

Gym editor/control panels are anchored to the top-left of the viewport and cover
the in-scene HUD labels (lives, power-ups, minerals). All gym panels should be
re-anchored to the bottom-left so the HUD stays visible.

## Problem statement

Every gym scene that exposes a plain-DOM tuning panel positions it at
`top: 8px; left: 8px` (`#gym-config-panel`) or `top: 8px; left: 260px`
(`#enemy-gym-panel`). The Phaser HUD renders its lives / power-up / weapon /
mineral rows at the top-left of the canvas (`HUD` is constructed at `(8, 8)`),
so the panel overlays the labels a designer is actively trying to read and tune
against. The original report called these "buttons"; the operator corrected this
to the lives/power-up labels.

## Users

- **Game designer / developer** tuning ship, enemy and boss configs in the gym
  scenes, who needs the live HUD (lives, active power-ups, weapons, minerals)
  visible while the tuning panel is open.
- **QA / playtester** verifying gym scenes, who needs both the HUD and the panel
  controls usable simultaneously.

### User stories

- As a designer tuning an enemy in the gym, I want the editor panel out of the
  way of the HUD so I can see lives/power-ups change as I tune.
- As a tester opening the Player gym, I want the tuning panel anchored
  consistently (bottom-left) across every gym scene.

## Acceptance criteria

- All gym panels are anchored to the **bottom-left** of the viewport instead of the top: `#gym-config-panel` (Player), `#enemy-gym-panel` (Enemies) and `#boss-gym-panel` (Boss), sharing consistent placement rules.
- Every panel has a `max-height` bounded to the viewport (minus a reserve) with internal vertical scrolling (`overflow-y: auto`), so a tall panel never extends above the viewport or re-covers the top-left HUD.
- With a panel open, the top-left HUD labels (lives / power-ups / weapons / minerals) are fully visible and unobscured.
- The in-canvas controls (`EXPLODE`, `SHOOT`, and the Boss `DAMAGE` button) and the status line are **repositioned to the bottom-right** so they remain visible and interactive while the panel occupies the bottom-left; the hint line stays clear of the panel.
- The Boss panel (`boss-gym-panel`, currently without any positioning CSS) receives the same bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` styling as the other panels.
- Automated tests assert the panels' bottom-left anchoring (e.g. via a shared CSS class/rule or computed style), the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control repositioning; testing/validation criterion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 and any Game Design Document references to the gym panel).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The game canvas is a fixed `960 × 540` design surface rendered with
  `Phaser.Scale.FIT`; DOM panels are `position: fixed`, in CSS pixels, and do
  **not** scale with the canvas.
- Panels are plain DOM appended to `#game-container`; each scene removes its
  panel on `SHUTDOWN` and clears stale panels on rebuild (test isolation).
- happy-dom (the test environment) performs no real layout, so tests cannot
  assert pixel geometry — they must assert the CSS rule/class or the intended
  inline style.
- No behavioural/API changes to panel contents; this is a presentation fix.
- The boss panel currently has class `gym-panel` but no CSS rule for it — this
  is a pre-existing gap to fold into the fix.

## Existing state

- `src/style.css`:
  - `#gym-config-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; ... }`
  - `#enemy-gym-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 260px; ... }`
  - No rule for `#boss-gym-panel` or `.gym-panel`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone HUD constructed at `(8, 8)` (top-left), depth
  `HUD_DEPTH` (1000).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — builds `#gym-config-panel`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — builds `#enemy-gym-panel` (~21 rows).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — builds `#boss-gym-panel` (spawn-interval control).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — places `EXPLODE` at `(10, 480)`,
  `SHOOT` at `(120, 480)`, status text at `(10, 504)`; creates the HUD.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — adds `DAMAGE` at `(240, 480)`.

## Desired change

Re-anchor every gym panel to the bottom-left of the viewport (shared class or
per-id rules), capped with a viewport-relative `max-height` and internal
scrolling so tall panels stay on-screen below the HUD. Apply consistent styling
to the currently-unstyled boss panel. Move the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/
`DAMAGE` controls and the status line to the bottom-right so they remain usable
alongside the panel. Update documentation and add regression tests for the
anchoring and control placement.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/style.css` — Move panel anchoring from `top` to `bottom`; add a shared
  `.gym-panel` rule (and/or `#boss-gym-panel`) so all panels share bottom-left
  placement plus a viewport-relative `max-height` with `overflow-y: auto`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — apply the shared panel class/id consistently
  (already sets `className = 'gym-panel'`); move the `DAMAGE` button to the
  bottom-right.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — reposition the in-canvas
  `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT` buttons and status line to the bottom-right; keep the hint
  line clear of the panel.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update §8.5 panel surface notes and
  the HUD-controls description (§ around line 156).
- Test files (e.g. `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`, `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymBoss.test.ts`, or a new `src/style.test.ts`) — assert bottom-left
  anchoring, the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control
  coordinates.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ** – Create E3 Tank gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** – Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 Gym surface — GymEnemies + editor panel)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bottom-left is free of HUD elements — the HUD is top-left, so
  this holds.
- **Risk:** the enemy editor panel is taller than the 540 px viewport; mitigated
  by the agreed `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto` (AC2).
- **Risk:** bottom-left is occupied by the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/`DAMAGE`
  controls; mitigated by the agreed bottom-right repositioning (AC4).
- **Risk:** bottom-right placement must not collide with the top-right
  `← INDEX` button or the centred hint line; verify when repositioning.
- **Risk:** happy-dom cannot verify real overlap; mitigation is to assert the
  anchoring rule/class and the control coordinates explicitly, and document the
  visual expectation for manual verification.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reworking panel layout/compaction beyond a height cap is
  a larger design task; record as a separate work item rather than folding into
  this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which UI element is actually being covered — which buttons?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "Buttons is the wrong word, it's actually the
  lives/powerup etc. labels." — i.e. the top-left HUD labels.
- **Q:** Does this affect only the Enemy gym scene or all gym scenes with a panel?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "all scenes with a panel (player too, for
  example)".
- **Q:** What should the fixed positioning be?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "move it so it is aligned bottom left".
- **Q:** The enemy editor panel is taller than the 540 px game viewport; how
  should tall panels be handled? **A (operator/producer, interactive):**
  "(1) a" — option (a) `max-height` + internal scroll.
- **Q:** Bottom-left is occupied by the `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/`DAMAGE` controls; how
  should the overlap be resolved? **A (operator/producer, interactive):**
  "(2) reposition to bottom right".

# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.

# Dedicated player-destruction SFX

## Goal
Add `playPlayerDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` — a heavier, layered,
player-specific cue distinct from the generic enemy `playDestructionSound()` —
plus unit tests. Wiring into scenes is a separate task that depends on the
composed juice helper.

## User story
As a player, losing my ship plays a distinct low "hull breach" boom instead of
the generic enemy pop, so a life lost reads differently from a kill.

## Scope
- New exported `playPlayerDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, built
  from the existing Web Audio helpers (`blip`) — no new binary assets.
  Proposed layers `[ASSUMPTION]`: (1) low impact thump, (2) descending body
  sweep, (3) short filtered-noise tail. Amplitude/length exposed as exported
  constants (e.g. `PLAYER_DESTRUCTION_*`).
- Extend `src/audio/effects.test.ts` with unit tests.

## Constraints
- Synthesis via Web Audio only; no asset pipeline.
- Must never throw when audio is unavailable (mirror existing safe patterns).
- Volume within the existing player-cue ceiling and documented.
- Do NOT modify `playDestructionSound()` behaviour (enemy + shield-absorb paths
  keep it).

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC3); GDD §7.3 Audio Direction.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` `blip()` and existing per-entity cues
  (`playTankDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `playPlayerDestructionSound()` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and is callable without an AudioContext without throwing.
- [ ] The cue is layered (≥ 2 oscillator blips) and its amplitude/length come from exported constants, not inline literals.
- [ ] Unit tests in `src/audio/effects.test.ts` assert layer count, constant-driven amplitude/duration, and that the cue differs from `playDestructionSound()` parameters.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is unchanged (its existing tests still pass).
- [ ] `npm test` passes and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — dedicated player-death SFX: a new playPlayerDestructionSound() is called exactly once.

# Intake Brief — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123)

- **Type:** feature
- **Priority:** medium
- **Status:** in-progress (intake)
- **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Asteroids are currently placed only as a single fixed formation group in
Level 1 Wave 1. The design calls for asteroids to be a persistent,
escalating roaming hazard: in **every** regular wave of every level, asteroids
should spawn at **random offscreen positions** and drift into the playfield,
with their **frequency growing slowly** as levels and waves progress. This
increases surviving pressure and variety without adding a new enemy archetype.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want asteroids to appear unpredictably from offscreen
  during every wave so that the playfield always carries a drifting hazard.
- **As a player**, I want the asteroid threat to grow slowly as I progress
  through levels and waves, so difficulty rises without sudden spikes.
- **As a player**, I want variety in asteroid size (more medium rocks early,
  more large rocks later), so the split-chain risk develops over a run.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` implements the E6 Asteroid: constant-velocity
  straight-line drift, four-edge wrap, continuous rotation, three size tiers
  (`large` / `medium` / `small`), split-on-destroy (large→2 medium→2 small),
  never fires. The constructor accepts optional `vx`/`vy` and `sizeTier`.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` places exactly one asteroid via
  `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, { startX: GAME_WIDTH * 0.6, startY: GAME_HEIGHT * 0.25 })`
  in Level 1 Wave 1 only. Every other wave has no asteroids.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` spawns wave groups from
  `WaveManager.planSpawns()`; asteroids roam via
  `Asteroid.updatePosition(dt)`, are shootable during transitions, survive
  wave timeouts, are cleared on boss entry, and are registered with
  `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn()` so wave-clear accounting includes them.
  `PlayScene` already exposes an injectable `rng` (`setRng`) and drives the
  simulation through the deterministic public `tick(dt)`.
- `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS = 30` (`PlayScene.ts`); each wave runs a 30 s
  countdown (`waveTimer`).
- No existing spawn-scheduler module; there is no test for random asteroid
  spawn timings or weight progression.

## Desired change

Add a **random offscreen asteroid spawner** that operates during every
regular wave. It is a pure planner (new `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) plus a
small `PlayScene` integration that releases planned spawns as the wave timer
elapses.

### Spawn plan (pure, RNG-injected)

For a given cumulative **global wave index** `g` (0-based across the whole
campaign, incremented once per regular wave):

1. **Per-wave count** starts at `2` and **doubles** each time the large weight
   threshold is reached: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.
2. **Size weighting** per wave:
   - medium weight is fixed at `80`;
   - large weight starts at `20` and increases by `+20` per wave;
   - when large weight reaches `2 × medium` (i.e. `160`), the weights **reset**
     to `medium 80 / large 20` and the per-wave count doubles.
   - Size tier is drawn per asteroid from these weights (baseline 80:20
     medium:large).
3. **Spawn timing** (fraction of `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS`):
   - `N` asteroids divide the wave into `N` equal segments;
   - anchor for asteroid `i` is `i / N`; a small random jitter (≈ ±5 %) is
     applied and clamped to `[0, 0.95]`;
   - the **first** asteroid is additionally constrained to the first `10 %`
     of the wave;
   - with the baseline `N = 2` this puts the first within 0–10 % and the
     second around 50 %.

### Offscreen origin and drift

- Choose a **random edge** uniformly from top / bottom / left / right.
- Place the asteroid at a random point along that edge, offset **outward**
  (offscreen) by `asteroid half-size + margin` so it is fully outside the
  viewport at spawn.
- Give it an **inward-directed** velocity (perpendicular to the edge, with up
  to ≈ ±30° spread) at the tier's canonical speed, guaranteeing the inward
  component dominates so it enters the playfield promptly.
- `Asteroid.vx`/`vy` continue to drive straight-line motion + four-edge wrap.

### Escalation semantics

- The global wave index is monotonic across the campaign; the large weight
  rises **once per wave**. Under the shipped 5-level campaign
  (2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 13 waves) the count is `2` for waves 0–6 and `4` for
  waves 7–12, with the weight cycle resetting at the count change.
- Boss encounter: **no** random asteroid spawns (existing boss-entry cleanup
  continues to destroy carried-over asteroids).

### Replacement of the fixed group

- Remove the fixed `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, …)` from Level 1 Wave 1 in
  `Formations.ts`; all asteroids now come from the random spawner. Update the
  existing `WaveManager.test.ts` assertion that Level 1 Wave 1 contains an
  asteroid group.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every regular wave of every level (Levels 1–5) spawns asteroids from the random offscreen spawner; the boss encounter spawns none.
- A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).
- Spawned asteroids are registered with `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns so wave-clear accounting includes them, and existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.
- The fixed asteroid group is removed from Level 1 Wave 1; all asteroids now originate from the spawner.
- Unit tests cover the pure planner deterministically (injected RNG): count progression, weight escalation/reset, timing segments, offscreen edge/position selection, and inward velocity. Integration tests in `PlayScene.test.ts` cover spawn timing against `tick(dt)`, offscreen positions, and boss exclusion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.1 / §4.2) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§1.2).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Pure logic must remain free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is
  unit-testable (mirror the `WaveManager` / `Formations` pattern).
- All randomness must flow through the scene's injectable `rng` to keep tests
  deterministic; the planner takes an `rng` parameter.
- Must not spawn while paused or during a wave/level transition, and must not
  break existing asteroid timeout/carry-over or boss-entry cleanup behaviour.
- Keep the spawner tuning in exported constants so it is easy to retune.
- Build → test → commit order only; no `main` branch changes (dev only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — **new** pure planner: weight escalation +
  count doubling, timing segments, offscreen edge/position + inward velocity.
- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.test.ts` — **new** deterministic unit tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — integrate the planner into `tick(dt)`; track
  elapsed wave time and release due spawns; extend `spawnAsteroidAt` (or add a
  helper) to accept velocity; skip paused/transition/boss phases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — integration tests (timing, offscreen,
  boss exclusion, dynamic registration).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — remove the fixed Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid group.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — add a pure `globalWaveIndex` accessor (or
  equivalent) so the planner can key escalation to campaign progress.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — update the Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid
  assertion.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — verify velocity injection path (no behaviour
  change expected).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` —
  document the new spawn mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** escalation is keyed to the cumulative global wave index
  across the campaign (not per-level resets), and the 13-wave shipped campaign
  reaches count 4 within a normal run.
- **Assumption:** "random edge" = uniform over the four screen edges; offscreen
  margin is a tunable constant (`half-size + small margin`).
- **Risk — wave stalls / asteroid accumulation:** more asteroids (plus large
  split chains = up to 7 kills each) can slow wave clearing, and asteroids
  survive timeouts and carry over, so their number can grow across waves.
  *Mitigation:* keep speeds slow, document tuning constants, and flag a
  possible concurrency cap / carry-over limit as a follow-up work item if
  playtesting shows a stall.
- **Risk — shallow inward velocity** could let an asteroid wrap before
  entering; *mitigation:* bias the velocity perpendicular to the spawn edge
  and clamp the angular spread.
- **Risk — non-determinism in tests:** *mitigation:* inject `rng` everywhere.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a concurrency cap, per-level resets, or UI for tuning
  are **out of scope** here; record any such opportunities as separate linked
  work items rather than expanding this item.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — Asteroids as an enemy (parent epic); established
  the entity, splitting, and wave integration.
- **AH-0MU8FORFF005RD9M** — PlayScene integration for asteroids.
- **AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L** — Asteroids survive wave timeout and carry over.
- **AH-0MUCG5TUG006I7X1** — Destroy carried-over asteroids on boss entry.
- **AH-0MUCG5T7S001F9MQ** — Keep asteroids moving/collidable during
  transitions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1.2 (Asteroid design) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 (E6 Asteroid), §4.2 (wave structures).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Weight scheduling and count progression:** "How should the large-weight
  increase work per step, and does count double (2→4→8) or increment
  (2→4→6)?" — **Answer (operator):** "as recommended". Accepted answer
  (recommended option): baseline medium:large = 80:20; increase large weight by
  +20 each wave (medium fixed at 80); when large reaches 2× medium (160:80),
  reset to 80:20 and double the per-wave count (2→4→8). Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q2 — Timing distribution for 4+ asteroids:** "For N asteroids per wave, how
  should spawn times distribute across the 30 s window?" — **Answer
  (operator):** "as recommended". Accepted answer (recommended option): first
  within 0–10 % of the wave timer; remaining N−1 distributed at ~equal
  intervals with ±5 % jitter so the mid-wave one lands near 50 %. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Existing fixed asteroid group:** "Should the current
  `group('asteroid','single',1)` in Level 1 Wave 1 be removed, with all
  asteroids now handled by the new random spawner?" — **Answer (operator):**
  "as recommended". Accepted answer: yes — replace entirely and update existing
  tests. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Scope of spawns:** "Should asteroids appear in every wave of every
  level?" — **Answer (operator):** "every wave of every level". Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Starting count and weighting:** spawn 2 per wave by default, weighted
  toward medium, escalating large weight with resets and count doubling. —
  **Answer (operator):** supplied in the same reply as Q4. Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q6 — Spawn edge:** "Which edge and position?" — **Answer (operator):**
  "random". Accepted answer: uniform random edge with inward drift. Source:
  interactive reply.

# Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Create `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — a pure (no Phaser dependency) planner module that computes when and where asteroids should spawn based on the global wave index.

## Module Structure

### Exported types

```typescript
export interface SpawnEvent {
  sizeTier: 'large' | 'medium';
  x: number;
  y: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
}
```

### Exported function

```typescript
export function computeSpawns(
  globalWaveIndex: number,
  gameWidth: number,
  gameHeight: number,
  waveTimeLimit: number,
  rng: () => number,
): SpawnEvent[];
```

## Algorithm (per spec)

### 1. Per-wave count

Start at 2. Every time the large weight reaches the reset threshold, double: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.

### 2. Size weighting

- Medium weight fixed at 80.
- Large weight starts at 20 and increases by +20 per wave.
- When large weight reaches 2 × medium (160), reset to 80:20 and double the count.

Formula: `largeWeight = min(20 + 20 * (globalWaveIndex % wavesPerReset), 160)` where `wavesPerReset` depends on when the reset threshold is hit.

### 3. Spawn timing

- Divide the wave into N equal segments (N = count).
- Anchor for asteroid i is `i / N`.
- Apply ±5% jitter, clamped to [0, 0.95].
- First asteroid constrained to first 10% of wave.
- Times must be ordered and non-duplicated.

### 4. Offscreen edge + velocity

- Choose random edge uniformly (top/bottom/left/right).
- Place asteroid at random point along that edge, offset outward by `halfSize + margin` so fully outside viewport.
- Give inward-directed velocity: perpendicular to spawn edge with ±30° spread, at the tier's canonical speed.
- The inward component must dominate so it enters the playfield promptly.

### 5. Tuning constants (exported for easy retuning)

```typescript
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_COUNT = 2;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_LARGE_WEIGHT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MEDIUM_WEIGHT = 80;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_INCREMENT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_RESET = 160;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.05;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MAX_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.95;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_FIRST_ASTEROID_MAX_FRACTION = 0.10;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_INWARD_ANGULAR_SPREAD = Math.PI / 6; // ±30°
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_OUTWARD_MARGIN = 10; // px beyond half-size
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `computeSpawns` returns exactly `count` events for any `globalWaveIndex >= 0`.
- Spawn count starts at 2 for `globalWaveIndex` 0–6, doubles at 7 (4), consistent with weight escalation.
- Large weight increases by +20 per wave; resets when it reaches 2× medium weight (160).
- First spawn time fraction is ≤ 0.10; subsequent times are spread across the wave with jitter.
- All spawn positions are fully offscreen (distance from viewport ≥ asteroid half-size + margin).
- All velocity vectors have inward components (toward the viewport centre).
- Output is deterministic for a given `globalWaveIndex`, dimensions, and RNG sequence.
- No Phaser runtime dependencies — pure TypeScript functions only.

- Covers parent AC2 — A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Covers parent AC3 — Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Covers parent AC4 — Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).

## Key Files

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — new module
data.title: Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
